actions.justification: Mandatory first action — assess neurological status in DKA patient. Altered mental status affects management decisions and is a key severity indicator.
Mandatory — must check potassium BEFORE starting insulin. K+ < 3.3 mEq/L is a contraindication to insulin initiation. Also needed to assess renal function, bicarbonate, and electrolytes.
Mandatory — baseline glucose required to assess DKA severity and guide insulin/dextrose management. Critical for monitoring in pregnant patient.
MANDATORY action with deadline of 60 minutes. Confirms DKA diagnosis and severity. Essential for monitoring resolution of ketosis in this pregnant patient with moderate DKA.

ADA guidelines mandate IV fluid resuscitation within 15 minutes (0.9% NaCl at 15-20 mL/kg/hr). Patient is hypotensive (BP 100/60, MAP 73) and tachycardic (HR 115), indicating volume depletion. Fluid resuscitation must precede insulin initiation.

Blood gas is needed to assess pH and bicarbonate level for DKA severity classification (moderate DKA: pH 7.00-7.24, bicarb 10-17). Also important in pregnancy as respiratory alkalosis compensates metabolic acidosis; RR of 28 (Kussmaul breathing) confirms need for pH monitoring.

Per ADA DKA guidelines, potassium replacement is required if K+ < 5.3 mEq/L before initiating insulin. This is standard practice in moderate DKA where total body potassium is depleted despite potentially normal serum levels. Insulin will further drive K+ intracellularly, risking dangerous hypokalemia.

BMP has been ordered (completed). Assuming K+ ≥ 3.3 mEq/L (as is typical in moderate DKA), insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr should be initiated now. DO NOT start if K+ < 3.3 — potassium replacement must occur first. This is the core treatment to reverse ketoacidosis and hyperglycemia, critical for maternal and fetal safety at 28 weeks.

ADA DKA guidelines require glucose monitoring every 1 hour during insulin infusion to guide rate adjustments and detect hypoglycemia, especially important in pregnancy where hypoglycemia carries fetal risk.

Patient has hypotension (BP 100/60) and tachycardia (HR 115), indicating ongoing volume depletion. Reassessing hydration status guides ongoing fluid replacement rate and type in this pregnant DKA patient.

Insulin infusion has been started, which drives potassium intracellularly. Serial potassium monitoring is critical to prevent dangerous hypokalemia, especially in pregnancy where maternal hypokalemia can affect fetal wellbeing.

Tracking the anion gap is essential to monitor DKA resolution. A closing anion gap indicates response to treatment. This is a key parameter alongside pH and bicarbonate for determining treatment progress.

Reassessing the anion gap is clinically indicated to trend DKA resolution. Serial anion gap monitoring helps confirm whether ketoacidosis is clearing in response to fluid resuscitation and insulin therapy already initiated.

Patient is 28 weeks pregnant with moderate DKA, RR 28, BP 100/60 suggesting hemodynamic stress. Bicarbonate may be considered if pH remains severely low (check blood gas results); pregnancy increases risk of fetal acidosis, making maternal pH optimization important. Administer only if pH <6.9 per ADA guidelines.

Mandatory action (★) - overdue at 70 minutes. Patient has tachycardia (HR 115), hypotension (BP 100/60), and tachypnea (RR 28); serial vital sign assessment is critical to monitor response to fluid resuscitation in this pregnant DKA patient.
Mandatory action (★) - required for IV fluid and medication administration. Must be confirmed/established to ensure ongoing fluid resuscitation and electrolyte replacement.

Mandatory action (★) - isotonic saline (0.9% NaCl) at 15-20 mL/kg/hr is the first-line treatment per ADA DKA guidelines. Patient has hypotension and tachycardia indicating volume depletion requiring immediate fluid resuscitation.

MANDATORY action per current phase. Serial ABG is required to monitor pH and bicarbonate to assess DKA severity and treatment response. Although order_lab_blood_gas was done, the system specifically requires 'order_lab_abg' as a distinct mandatory action. Critical in pregnancy as respiratory alkalosis compensates for metabolic acidosis — serial monitoring is essential.
Calculating the anion gap is essential to assess severity of DKA and monitor for resolution. BMP has been ordered; calculating anion gap helps guide ongoing management and insulin infusion titration.

Assessing anion gap closure is a key endpoint for DKA resolution. With insulin infusion already started, monitoring for anion gap closure guides decisions about transitioning to subcutaneous insulin and discontinuing infusion.
Labs and blood gas results are pending/available now at 100 minutes; formal DKA severity classification should be performed to guide ongoing management intensity and disposition decisions.

Pregnant patient at 28 weeks with moderate DKA (HR 115, BP 100/60, RR 28, on insulin infusion) requires ICU-level monitoring for both maternal and fetal wellbeing, continuous insulin infusion management, and close electrolyte monitoring.
